doc.title: Joe LaBarbera interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 15, 2021

title: Following his brothers to college and Berklee standing
summary: College was the path everyone took; at Berklee he stood out alongside Harvey Mason and Peter Donald.

venues.name: State University of New York at Potsdam

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Where they grew up. So we were in Rochester so I never knew that I was traveling through a town that had a famous band. Did the idea of pursuing a music career necessarily include college?

I think the college aspect of it was simply the road that everyone was taking. You know all of my classmates were going on to college. Pat and John had previously enrolled in State University of New York at Potsdam, and they both — Pat transferred out of there and went to Berklee College in Boston. So yes, I think it was simply that I was following my brothers once again, whatever path they would take I was going to take it. And I’m pretty sure I knew at least enough to know that I didn’t know much and I needed more.
That’s a good thing to know.
The idea of going to school and sort of jockeying in position with the other drummers, and where did you fall in that hierarchy?

Pretty good actually, right away. I mean Harvey Mason and I, he was a year ahead of me but we were the two guys basically from our generation. The real guy was Peter Donald, who was three years our senior at that point. So he was getting ready to graduate when I got to Berklee but I was known right away because I could play a little bit. You know I could play pretty good time and I knew tunes. So that’s really all it was about and then I wanted to play all the time as did everyone else, so —
